narrative:
On November 5, 2026, the Karnataka High Court conducted hearings for 1,184 out of 3,330 scheduled cases, achieving an overall hearing rate of 35.6%. This represents a drop from the 40.5% clearance rate recorded on November 4 and 41.8% on November 2, though it remains above the 30.1% rate observed on November 3. The decline occurred alongside an increase in total scheduled matters, which rose to 3,330 from 3,167 on the previous day.

Bench-level efficiency varied significantly across court halls. High conversion rates were reported by Justice H.P. Sandesh (75.4%, 49 of 65 cases), Justice V Srishananda (70.2%, 59 of 84 cases), and the division bench of D K Singh & H. Shanthi Bhushan (67.5%, 27 of 40 cases). In contrast, several heavy lists saw minimal clearance: T.P. Vivekananda's bench in Hall 2A heard none of its 293 listed matters, while B M Shyam Prasad's bench in Hall 7 converted 5.3% (7 of 133 cases).

Stage-wise analysis reveals that Preliminary Hearings led major procedural categories with a 51.6% hearing rate (226 of 438 cases), whereas Final Hearing conversion dropped to 20.8% (125 of 601 cases) from 29.4% yesterday. Orders matters comprised the largest share of scheduled work (1,299 cases) but reached a 31.9% hearing rate. By case type, Writ Petitions (WP) dominated the docket with 1,264 listings and a 36.2% hearing rate, while Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) and Civil Miscellaneous Petitions (CMP) logged higher clearance rates of 59.1% and 62.0%, respectively.
